dalia.section: 2.2.4 Data Synchronisation and Ground Truth Generation
findings: Authors report initial automated ECG R-peak detection followed by manual addition and removal of peaks.
Start and end double-tap acceleration patterns align devices and correct drift; no millisecond precision guarantee is reported.
Released PKLs contain rpeaks in the 700 Hz chest ECG time base; this work retains original annotations, reports duplicate entries, and derives a unique-event view without using PPG predictions.
No beat-type labels establish normal-to-normal intervals; no independent expert re-adjudication was performed in this PoC.
Cross-device offline alignment is reported with approximately 33 ms accuracy.
Baseline reference beats are automatic ECG detections; no manually adjudicated PPG peak truth is published.
This work retains the original official unfiltered ECG peak sequence for interval calculation. It does not concatenate quotient-filtered peaks.
WFDB XQRS agreement in fixed blocks is a conservative ECG-only availability screen. Agreement does not prove correctness, and disagreement can reject usable ECG.

notes: 42 mostly high-quality anaesthesia acquisitions including adults and children; sensor/site differs from wrist PPG.
Official converter says PPG peak annotations exist but their manual status was not verified in this review, so no data were downloaded or claimed as manual PPG truth.
BUT-PPG full resource was provisioned by the parallel SQI task; not required to replace DaLiA wrist reference.
